# Parity-forest cap transport: a valid basin invariant and an exact obstruction

Let `J` be a finite lattice-convex set of integer indices. Suppose every
parity class has a designated representative `p_r in J`, and

    Q=conv{p_r}, Q intersect Z^n={p_r}.

The map `R(z)=(z+p_[z mod 2])/2` takes `J` into `J`. Suppose in addition
there are supporting inequalities `a_s dot z<=beta_s` with equality at
`p_s` and strict inequality at every other representative. These are the
relations furnished by the full-parity case of the expanded-facet witness
construction.

## Exact orbit and cap consequences

Distance to `Q` contracts by a factor at least two under `R`: if `q in Q`
is nearest to `z`, then `(q+p_[z mod2])/2 in Q`, so

    dist(Rz,Q)<=dist(z,Q)/2.

The orbit stays in the finite set `J`. Positive distances to `Q` in that
finite set have a positive minimum. Thus the orbit eventually enters
`Q intersect J`, where it reaches a representative and stays fixed.
Every target has at most `2^n` preimages, since a preimage with parity
`r` must equal `2w-p_r`.

Write an orbit as `z_0=z,z_{j+1}=Rz_j`, reaching `z_k=p_s` for the first
time, and put `r_j=z_j mod2`. Iterating its affine recurrence gives

    p_s=2^{-k}z+sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^{j-k}p_{r_j},
    z-p_s=sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^j(p_s-p_{r_j}).         (1)

Consequently each basin belongs to its root's expanded facet exterior:

    a_s dot z>=beta_s,

with strict inequality for every nonroot in that basin. If all digits
equaled `s`, (1) would force `z=p_s`; otherwise one strictly positive
support difference appears in (1). In a grouped cap certificate with
original threshold `h_s<beta_s`, its own group therefore covers every
continuous fiber in its basin.

For convex fibers `K_z`, the exact iterated Minkowski inclusion is

    2^{-k}K_z+sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^{j-k}K_{p_{r_j}}
       subset K_{p_s}.                            (2)

This follows by induction from each midpoint inclusion. Repeated
Brunn-Minkowski gives the corresponding inequality for volume roots.
It does not make the different sets arriving at a root disjoint.

If anchor points `g_r in K_{p_r}` are chosen, (2) yields a deterministic
map from each source fiber to its root fiber:

    T_z(x)=2^{-k}x+sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^{j-k}g_{r_j}.

For any affine halfspace margin `L`, its value at the transported point
is the same convex combination of the original source margin and anchor
margins. Thus if a halfspace contains a transported point, it contains
the source point or at least one anchor. This is a valid point-incidence
statement. It is not a volume bound, because a small-volume anchor fiber
can be used by an arbitrarily larger source fiber, and different arriving
copies can coincide. The counterexample below makes both failures exact.

## A six-fiber full-parity example

Work with `n=d=2`. The integer projection is the polygon

    z_1>=0, z_2>=0, |z_1-z_2|<=1, z_1+z_2<=3.

Its integer points are exactly

    J={(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}.

Take the four binary points as representatives for their own parities.
Their convex hull is the empty integer unit square. The associated map
is coordinatewise `R(z)=ceil(z/2)`, so

    R(2,1)=R(1,2)=(1,1).

All four representatives are fixed. Therefore the basin of `(1,1)` is
precisely `{(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}`.

Let the affine continuous center map be

    b(z)=(11-4z_1-4z_2, 4z_1-5).

The three basin centers are respectively

    b(1,1)=(3,-1), b(2,1)=(-1,3), b(1,2)=(-1,-1).

For those three indices use squares of radius `1/10` in the continuous
`ell_infinity` norm. At the other three roots use squares of radius
`1/100`. Let `K_z` denote these six squares, and define

    C=conv(union_{z in J} {z}xK_z).

This is a bounded full-dimensional convex polytope in `R^4`. Its fibers
at the five projection vertices are the prescribed squares by extremality
of those vertices. Its only other integer fiber is `(1,1)`, where it
contains the prescribed large square and cannot exceed it: the center
map is affine and every generating radius is at most `1/10`.
Hence its mixed set has exactly the six prescribed fibers. Their areas
are

    V=1/25=100/2500 for each basin fiber,
    v=1/2500 for each other root.

The total mass is `M=303/2500`, and the root-11 basin mass is
`M_11=3/25`.

## Four compatible positive circuits and common real contacts

Use continuous normals

    u_1=(1,0), u_2=(0,1), u_3=(-1,-1)

in all four groups, with the following common terms:

    ell_00(z)=1/100-(z_1+z_2)/10,
    ell_10(z)=(z_1-z_2)/10-1/20,
    ell_01(z)=(z_2-z_1)/10-1/20,
    ell_11(z)=(z_1+z_2)/10-1/10.

Define twelve closed caps, three per group, by

    H_{s,j}={u_j dot x+ell_s(z)>=0}.               (3)

Their continuous normals have the minimal positive dependence with all
multipliers `1/3`, of rank two. Writing `ell_s=a_s dot z-h_s`, their
original projected inequalities are `a_s dot z<=h_s`. Their complementary
auxiliary polytope is

    Q_aux={u_j dot x+ell_s(z)<=0 for all s,j}.

Its integer-coordinate projection is exactly

    1/10<=z_1+z_2<=1, |z_1-z_2|<=1/2.            (4)

Necessity follows by summing each positive circuit; sufficiency follows
by choosing `x=0`. Region (4) is bounded and has no integer point: its
coordinate ranges lie inside `[-1/5,3/4]`, so the only possible integer
point would be `(0,0)`, excluded by the lower sum constraint. The
continuous fibers of `Q_aux` are bounded triangles, since the three
continuous normals positively span `R^2`; the right sides are uniformly
bounded over (4). Strict inequalities hold at `z=(11/40,11/40),x=0`.
Thus `Q_aux` is bounded, full-dimensional, and globally mixed-integer-free.

The four contact projections may be chosen as

    r_00=(1/20,1/20),
    r_10=(5/8,1/8),
    r_01=(1/8,5/8),
    r_11=(1/2,1/2).

At each contact `q_s=(r_s,0)`, all three inequalities of its own group
are equalities and every other group's inequalities are strict. Hence
all common-contact and cross-contact conditions hold exactly.

Expand the four projected offsets to

    beta_00=0, beta_10=beta_01=1/10, beta_11=1/5.

Each original `h_s` is strictly smaller. The four binary representatives
are respectively strict exclusive facet witnesses: their own equality
holds and all other expanded inequalities are strict. The expanded
polyhedron has no point of `J` in its interior; roots lie on its facets,
and the two remaining indices violate its sum facet. This verifies the
full-parity witness geometry used to construct the forest.

## Exact failure of basin mass promotion

For every group `s`, the three caps in (3) have exactly the same cap
color allocation:

* cap 1 contains the large fiber `(1,1)` and all three small root fibers;
* cap 2 contains only the large fiber `(2,1)`;
* cap 3 contains only the large fiber `(1,2)`.

All containment and exclusion margins are strict. One direct check is
that all common terms over `J` lie between `-29/100` and `1/5`.
At the three large-square centers the indicated normal has positive
margin at least `18/10-29/100>0`, while each unintended normal has
margin at most `-9/10+1/5<0`. The small-root centers are `(11,-5)`,
`(7,-1)`, and `(7,-5)`; with their radius `1/100`, the first normal remains
strictly positive and the other two remain strictly negative throughout
their squares. Checking vertices suffices because all margins are affine.

Therefore, for every group,

    mu(H_{s,1})=103/2500,
    mu(H_{s,2})=mu(H_{s,3})=100/2500.              (5)

But

    gamma_2 M_11=(4/9)(3/25)=4/75,
    4/75-103/2500=91/7500>0.                      (6)

Thus the tempting inequality

    max_j mu(H_{s,j})>=gamma_d mu(basin s)

is false. This counterexample retains the full-parity graph, all strict
expanded-facet witnesses, a bounded convex source body, all positive
circuits, all attained real contacts, and all cross-contact inequalities.
It is not merely an unstructured decimation example.

All twelve cap masses are below, for example, `T=104/2500`, so a common
strict cap budget exists. That budget is **not** below the OC target
`gamma_2 M/4`; the example does not satisfy a hypothesized violation of
OC. It refutes the proposed basin promotion as an auxiliary inequality,
not OC or the possibility of a different global use of the small budget.

## Coincident images and arbitrarily small anchor budgets

The two nonroot midpoint inclusions are

    (K_(2,1)+K_(0,1))/2 subset K_(1,1),
    (K_(1,2)+K_(1,0))/2 subset K_(1,1).

Both Minkowski midpoint sets are exactly the same square: their center
is `(3,-1)` and their radius is `(1/10+1/100)/2=11/200`.
Consequently their volumes cannot be added inside the root fiber.

If just the small-fiber centroids are used as anchor points, both
transport maps have the same image square, centered at `(3,-1)` with
radius `1/20`. It lies entirely in cap 1. Yet the two source fibers lie
entirely in cap colors 2 and 3. The incidence implication is paid for
by the two anchors, each lying in cap 1, rather than by source cap mass.
Replacing every small radius by a positive parameter `epsilon` tending
to zero preserves every strict relation above. The two incoming source
areas remain `V`, while each anchor area is `4 epsilon^2`; the incoming
mass divided by the available anchor mass is unbounded. Bounded graph
indegree alone therefore cannot control this anchor charge.

All arithmetic and the exact polytope/incidence checks are verified by
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_parity_forest_cap_transport.py`.
